transcript: ProxyMe runs as a web app with a React frontend and a Flask backend connected to a PostgreSQL database. The backend receives cumulative transcript segments from a meeting platform and uses an LLM to generate either short meeting updates or deferrals, then sends these messages back to the user interface in near real time. This creates a live feedback loop between the meeting, the agent, and the user, supporting continuous engagement.

transcript: Across all dependent variables, we saw no clear single winner, but large variance between participants and contexts. We observed clear trade-offs. Frequent low-detail updates increased presence but also workload, while infrequent detailed updates reduced disruption but weakened engagement. Similarly, multiple-choice responses were fast but limiting, while text input offered agency at a higher effort cost. Participants valued these trade-offs differently. Importantly, participant experiences also shifted with meeting relevance and topic familiarity. This suggests that we should treat partial participation as a spectrum.
